items.issue: The DP row in Table 10-1 describes only training DP (replicates optimizer, all-reduces gradients). The chapter text (§1, §2, §3, §6) explicitly and repeatedly distinguishes training DP from inference DP (independent replicas, no gradient sync, no optimizer). items.issue: The CP row specifies 'ring' as the communication pattern, but the chapter text (§1 item 5) only says CP 'splits the sequence dimension across GPUs' and never establishes a ring collective for CP. Ring is one possible implementation; Megatron-style sequence parallelism typically uses all-gather/reduce-scatter, and inference KV sharding can use various patterns. Introducing 'ring' in the table without textual support is an unsupported specificity.

items.issue: The caption is extremely long (~150 words) and contains three distinct layers of commentary: (1) a description of the three panels, (2) a communication-specificity note about TP collectives and PP microbatch scheduling, and (3) a grayscale accessibility note. The communication-specificity note is substantive content that belongs in the prose, not the caption. The grayscale note is a production note that belongs in a figure note or the production spec.
items.quoted_clause: Communication-specificity note: the TP collective is algorithm-dependent — a plain all-reduce of partial sums is one option, but fused kernels often use reduce-scatter + all-gather (or a single all-reduce) depending on the framework; the PP bubble size depends on microbatch scheduling (more microbatches shrink the bubble but add memory). The panels show the canonical configuration (TP all-reduce per layer; PP with a small fixed microbatch count; GPU counts and layer ranges schematic — the canonical host is 8×H100 and the canonical 70B has 80 layers); substitute the actual collective and schedule for the target stack. Grayscale note: each box's text label carries its role, so the in-figure color key (blue = weights · orange = GPU · green = data · red = comms) is redundant, not load-bearing.
items.fix_instruction: Move the communication-specificity note to the prose paragraph after the figure and the grayscale note to a figure note/production spec; keep a concise (≤60-word) panel description plus the [ILLUSTRATIVE] label.
items.evidence: Caption located by flexible search and measured: 211 words (finding said ~150 — it is longer), containing all three layers: panel description, '**Communication-specificity note:**' and '**Grayscale note:** ... redundant, not load-bearing'. items.evidence: Both fragments found in chapter-10.md L169: 'the total expert residency that must be sharded' and 'since the full expert set occupies HBM even when only a fraction is routed per token'. items.issue: The remedy list includes 'more efficient attention implementations' for a shortfall that the paragraph has just shown is a *compute* shortfall against the theoretical peak. FlashAttention-style kernels reduce HBM traffic and improve achieved efficiency; they do not reduce the 2 x params x tokens FLOP floor that already exceeds peak. The same confusion recurs in §6, where 'kernel fusion (flash-attention, scaled-dot-product attention with fewer reads)' is listed as a lever under 'prefill in the compute-bound regime'.
items.quoted_clause: "Therefore one H100 cannot satisfy the stated prefill budget under these assumptions. ... Meeting the latency SLO therefore calls for multiple GPUs (model parallelism or data parallelism) or more efficient attention implementations."
items.fix_instruction: In Ch 2 §3/§6, replace "more efficient attention implementations" / flash-attention in the compute-bound lists with constraint-matched levers (more GPUs, lower-precision path with higher tensor-core peak, smaller model, fewer tokens), and move attention-kernel work to the bandwidth-side regime where the book's own §1 framing says it helps.
items.evidence: Both quotes found verbatim in design/manuscript/chapter-02/chapter-02.md §3: "With $1.19 > 0.989$ ... this first-order lower bound already exceeds the H100's theoretical peak. Therefore one H100 cannot satisfy the stated prefill budget under these assumptions." and "Meeting the latency SLO therefore calls for multiple GPUs (model parallelism or data parallelism) or more efficient attention implementations." §6 repeats the pattern: "**With prefill in the compute-bound regime → optimization levers:** kernel fusion (flash-attention, scaled-dot-product attention with fewer reads), model parallelism..., more GPUs in parallel...". The physics claim holds: the shortfall is against theoretical peak FLOPs (1.29 PFLOP / 1.08 s ≈ 1.19 PFLOPS > 0.989 PFLOPS, printed in-source), and attention kernels reduce HBM traffic, not the 2×params×tokens FLOP floor — the book's own §1 framework undercuts the remedy: "FlashAttention moves the bottleneck from *bandwidth* toward *compute* (fewer HBM round-trips)" (it helps when bandwidth binds; here compute already binds). §6 even states "Lowering precision ... does *not* reduce the underlying algorithmic operation count (the usual 2 × params × tokens FLOPs...)" while still listing flash-attention as a compute-bound lever.
